Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mention verb and noun

also make mention of, reference, make reference to, touch on, since mention has been made of

classical

Cic. Att. 6.1.8: in quā nōn ejus mentiōnem faciās
Plaut. Most. 813: nōlī facere mentiōnem tē hās ēmisse
Traupman 43: Nōlī dē autumnō mentiōnem mihi facere

mentiōnem facere

mentiō, mentiōnis f., with faciō, facere, fēcī, factum; what is mentioned in the genitive, or dē and the ablative

mention, make mention of

What is mentioned goes in the genitive (Epicūrī mentiōnem facis, Cic. Att. 14.20.5) or takes dē and the ablative; Plautus also has an accusative and infinitive. The person told takes cum: fac mentiōnem cum avonculō, “mention it to my uncle” (Plaut. Aul. 685). Passive: quoniam facta lituī mentiō est, “since the trumpet has been mentioned” (Gell. 5.8.8).

Other words

  • commemorō, commemorāre, commemorāvī, commemorātum — mention, bring up, recount

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 71: nōn commemorāre quī contulit

    Lewis & Short: “to make mention of something, to recount, relate”; of bringing a thing up in speech, often in some detail.

  • meminī, meminisse — mention (in speaking or writing)

    verb, defective; the genitive, or dē and the ablative · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.108.1 (Lewis & Short): Achillam, cujus suprā meminimus; Cic. Phil. 2.91: meministī ipse dē exsulibus

    Lewis & Short: “rare but class.” in this sense; usually “remember” (see remember).

  • attingō, attingere, attigī, attāctum — touch on, mention briefly

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.201: perquam breviter perstrīnxī atque attigī; M-O s.v. passing

    In passing: in trānsitū attingere, after Quintilian’s quae librō quīntō leviter in trānsitū attigeram (7.3.27, quoted by Morgan–Owens).

  • nōminō, nōmināre, nōmināvī, nōminātum — mention by name

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 6 (Lewis & Short): quem honōris causā nōminō; Traupman 103, 345: eum nōlō nōmināre, I don’t want to mention him by name

Examples

  • nōlī facere mentiōnem tē hās ēmisse

    don’t mention that you’ve bought the housePlaut. Most. 813

  • flēns mihi meam fāmam commendāstī; quae epistula tua est in quā nōn ejus mentiōnem faciās?

    In tears you begged me to look after my good name: is there a single letter of yours in which you don’t mention it?Cic. Att. 6.1.8

  • odiōsum sānē genus hominum officia exprobrantium; quae meminisse dēbet is in quem conlāta sunt, nōn commemorāre quī contulit

    A tiresome sort, those who throw their favours in your face: the one who received them should remember them, the one who did them should not bring them up.Cic. Amic. 71

  • Quoniam nummōrum mentiō facta est …

    Since money has been mentioned …Traupman 103

See also mean, say, talk, remember.
